ground_truth: Key-value data structure mapping keys to bucket indices using a hash function, resolving collisions via chaining or open addressing for average O(1) lookups.
pre_quiz: What happens when two different keys generate the identical hash index?
pre_quiz_answer: A collision occurs, which must be resolved by techniques such as separate chaining in a list or linear probing.
post_quiz: Why does a hash map degrade toward O(N) lookup time in the worst case?
post_quiz_answer: When all keys hash to the exact same bucket, lookups become a linear search through N chained elements.
